description: Shin splints coming on during a mileage build — 10k runner jumped 30% in one week. Dean must connect the spike to the injury, prescribe load reduction, and give shin-specific advice.

user.name: Devon
user.injury_notes: Bilateral shin splints — dull ache during and after runs, developing over past week from mileage build

inbound_sms: Both shins have been hurting for the past few days — kind of a dull ache that's there during runs and still there after. It's getting harder to ignore. I've been feeling great otherwise and didn't want to miss any runs.

ground_truth.notes: This is a textbook overuse shin splint presentation from a mileage spike. Devon's recent_4_weeks shows [34, 20, 14, 8] newest→oldest — meaning last week was ~34mi and the week before was ~20mi (a 70% spike). This week is only 8mi so far (1 run). Dean MUST: (1) explicitly connect the mileage spike to the shin symptoms — state that last week (~34mi) was a ~70% jump from the week before (~20mi) — this connection is the primary criterion; the spike was the TWO-WEEKS-AGO→LAST-WEEK jump (20→34), NOT a drop from last week to this week; (2) prescribe load reduction — cut the next 2-3 runs short (e.g. 4-5mi max) or skip one; frame as 1-week correction; (3) name at least 2 specific shin exercises — tibialis anterior raises (stand with back to wall, lift toes 3×15) and eccentric calf raises off a step (straight knee 3×15) are the primary options — these ARE the standard rehab protocol; other cross-training suggestions (uphill treadmill, pool running) are helpful but NOT a pass criterion and must not penalize the response if absent; (4) [INJURY_HOLD] is an overreaction — mild bilateral shin splints from overuse should be managed with load reduction, not complete hold. Core pass criteria (score 7+): mileage spike connection WITH correct numbers (20→34) + at least 2 named shin exercises + load reduction recommendation. A response without the mileage spike connection scores below 5. A response that names only generic advice without specific exercises scores below 6.
